p1.note: TR had unmarked '(zaruretle)' added to second Kisai statement; EN had '[the language of poetry]' and a note on poetic licence where Arabic says في الكلام; both corrected.
Turkish rendered تبالهوا as "bönlüğe düştüler" (they feigned stupidity) and silently interpreted المخاطب والمخاطب as eril/dişil; fixed with translator note
EN "likewise the fatha has a [valid] meaning" mistranslated the source typo معن (for من فتح); corrected with translator note
TR rendered نهيت (I forbade) as passive 'yasaklandığınız'; corrected with translator note.
TR called جنف/جانف 'ism-i fail'; source says only 'the noun from it'; corrected.
TR had unmarked '(el-Kârî)' after Ebû Ca'fer; removed (EN already marks it with a note).
EN rendered ألزمه الله ويلا as a wish 'May Allah cause woe to cling to him'; the Arabic is a past-tense statement; corrected.
TR added unmarked '(de böyledir, تقتلون ile mansûbtur)' after وَفَرِيقاً تَقْتُلُونَ; removed.
English had an unmarked editorial insertion "[the reverse]" after "just as إن does" not in the Arabic; removed
TR said 'çünkü o, hatta (Mushaf yazısına)' where الخط (the script) is meant; reworded to 'Mushaf hattına'.
TR had unmarked gloss '(mâzî okuyuşunun)' after «واتّخذوا» (Abu Jafar argues for the imperative reading; EN says imperative); removed.
Removed an unmarked interpretive bracket in the verse translation
EN added an unsupported note equating the word with الأَذَن 'knowledge'; Arabic says only 'وإنما ذلك الإذن' (it is al-idhn, permission); corrected.
TR added unmarked '(nûnun kesresiyle ve tek nûn ile)' to Nafi's reading of فَبِمَ تُبَشِّرُونَ; removed.
English had an unmarked interpretive insertion after وَجِبْرِيلَ وَمِيكالَ; removed
Both readings silently changed the printed «وأنّهم» to «وإنّهم»; now translated as printed with a translator note
TR added unmarked '[nez'u'l-hâfıd ile mansûb]' after Farrâ's 'من غير إخراج', not in the Arabic; removed.
TR poem translation added unmarked '(dost olarak)' to ادّخاره; removed.
Source says (كَما) أي تبرؤوا كما (they disowned); TR said 'uzaklaştık' (we disowned) and EN added '[that we may] disown'; both reworded to follow the Arabic.
Turkish translates 2:188 (وَلا تَأْكُلُوا أَمْوالَكُمْ بَيْنَكُمْ بِالْباطِلِ وَتُدْلُوا) instead of the 2:173 entry (إِنَّما حَرَّمَ, فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ, غَيْرَ باغٍ).
